# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 11

**11:1** And she took the water-jar and went out to draw water. And behold, a voice said to her: "Hail, highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women."

**11:2** And she looked to the right and to the left to see where this voice came from. Trembling, she went back into her house and set down the water-jar, took up the purple thread, sat down in her seat, and drew it out.

**11:3** And behold, an angel of the Lord stood before her and said: "Do not fear, Mary, for you have found grace before the Lord of all. You shall conceive by his word."

**11:4** And she, hearing this, reasoned within herself, saying: "Shall I conceive by the Lord, the living God, and give birth as every woman gives birth?"

**11:5** And the angel of the Lord said: "Not so, Mary. For the power of the Lord shall overshadow you; wherefore the holy one who shall be born of you shall be called Son of the Most High. And you shall call his name Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins."

**11:6** And Mary said: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord before him. Let it be to me according to your word."

---

## Translator's Note

The Annunciation in the Protevangelium is in two stages: a disembodied voice at the well (11:1-2), then the angel in person at home (11:3-6). The first voice is an auditory annunciation without visual presence — a theophanic device common in later Jewish literature. Mary's return to the purple thread between the two encounters frames the Annunciation within the temple-veil work: she is weaving the sacred curtain and will become the vessel of the sacred incarnation simultaneously. Her fiat in 11:6 is the direct source of Luke 1:38.
